title: WAF: rules, rate limiting and managed rule groups

videos.script: Alarms tell you about damage that already happened. A firewall refuses the request before it reaches the application. {{refuse}} AWS WAF reads every request in front of a load balancer: its address, its path, its headers. It runs a web ACL, a list of rules in priority order, and the first rule that blocks decides. {{acl}} You will build the shop's: a list of addresses to refuse, a rate limit on the login page, and a group of rules that AWS writes and keeps current. {{rules}} You will meet the lock token, which stops two people from overwriting each other's change. {{lock}} You will learn to start every new rule in Count, so it is tested on the logs and not on customers. {{count}} And you will price it from the public list: five dollars a web ACL, a dollar a rule, sixty cents per million requests, and what changes that last number. {{price}} One honest note before starting. The lab stores the web ACL and inspects no traffic. What a rule would match comes from AWS's documentation, and from the logs on a real account. {{honest}}
